first.rationale: Competitor entry pricing creates an immediate, consequential acquisition risk in the price-sensitive SMB segment, making targeted promotional pricing the leading current intervention. Verify the pricing evidence first because sustainable qualified revenue—not acquisition alone—is the objective and discounting can impair downstream value; verify onboarding evidence because completion has also declined and it is the strongest competing direct lever. Run only a targeted SMB experiment with qualified-revenue and post-promotion retention guardrails rather than broadly discounting.

final.rationale: Run the shortened-onboarding experiment. It directly addresses the 4% completion decline and the 6% activation decline, while the verified source showed higher completion, faster time-to-value, and a +3% 30-day retention lift. Do not use promotional pricing: its verified qualified-revenue lift came with a -12% 30-day retention result and was explicitly judged unsustainable. Evaluate onboarding on qualified revenue and retention, with guardrails for account quality and sales qualification.
